activities.name: Whelan's
activities.short_description: A long-running Dublin pub and live-music venue with gigs, indie club nights, karaoke and other late-night events across several rooms.
activities.why_it_fits: It offers students a flexible central-Dublin night out: low-cost club or karaoke options as well as live gigs, with a social atmosphere and varied music programming.
activities.cost_basis: The official events calendar read on 2026-10-08 listed examples from €5 karaoke and €10 club nights to €11–€19.65 live events; the exact price depends on the selected event.
activities.additional_potential_costs: Drinks, food, transport and any booking or service fees may cost extra.
activities.approximate_duration: About 2–4 hours for a typical gig or club night; duration varies by event and is not fixed by the venue.
activities.availability: Date-dependent. The official calendar read on 2026-10-08 showed recurring karaoke and indie-club nights plus separately ticketed live events, but line-ups, times, prices and availability can change. Confirm the chosen event directly with Whelan's.
activities.booking_needed: Depends on the event: book ahead for ticketed gigs where possible; some club nights are explicitly listed as door-only. Check the official event listing before travelling.
activities.energy_level: Medium to high, depending on whether you choose a seated/listening gig or a late club night.
activities.social_format: Good for going with friends, meeting other music fans and enjoying a shared live-event or club atmosphere; solo attendance is also possible.
activities.transport_suitability: Public transport is the practical choice from DCU Glasnevin. Cycling is possible with your own route and parking plan; walking is not practical for most students. The venue is in central Dublin and is about a 10-minute walk from St Stephen's Green, according to Ticketmaster.
activities.what_to_bring: Photo ID, since Ticketmaster states the venue is strictly over 18s; bring your ticket or booking confirmation if required, and a charged phone.
activities.caveat: Whelan's is an over-18 venue. This is a venue/activity listing rather than a promise of a particular gig; event schedules, entry rules, prices, opening hours and availability are changeable, so verify the official listing before going.
activities.confidence: High for venue identity, address, age restriction and the date-checked event examples; medium for general duration and transport suitability because these depend on the chosen night and route.
activities.official_source_title: Whelan's | Dublin's Best Live Music Venue

activities.name: The Workman's Club
activities.short_description: A Temple Bar live-entertainment venue hosting gigs, comedy, arts events, showcases and indie club nights in a historic building.
activities.why_it_fits: It offers varied, student-friendly nightlife in one venue, from gigs and comedy to club nights, making it easy to match different music and social interests.
activities.location: 10 Wellington Quay, Dublin 2, beside The Clarence in Temple Bar
activities.cost_basis: There is no single venue admission price: the official site lists different events, and ticket prices vary by event; check the specific event listing before going.
activities.additional_potential_costs: Transport, drinks, and any food or event-specific booking fees may be extra.
activities.approximate_duration: Event-dependent; allow roughly the length of the chosen gig, comedy night or club night, as stated by the organiser.
activities.availability: The venue runs a changing programme of live music, comedy, arts events, showcases and club nights. Dates, times, age rules, ticketing and availability change by event, so check the official listing for the date you want.
activities.booking_needed: Event-dependent: book tickets in advance when the chosen listing requires or recommends it; do not assume walk-in entry.
activities.energy_level: Medium to high, depending on the event; standing, late-night and club events can be especially energetic.
activities.social_format: Best as a small-group or sociable night out; the programme is built around shared live music, comedy and arts experiences.
activities.transport_suitability: Suitable for public transport, cycling and walking from central Dublin; walking is possible from DCU Glasnevin but is a substantial cross-city trip, so public transport or cycling is more practical for most students. Check the route and late-night options for the specific event.
activities.what_to_bring: Event ticket or booking confirmation if required, phone, payment card, and a light layer; bring ear protection if you are sensitive to loud music.
activities.caveat: This is a venue rather than one fixed activity. Do not treat the venue description as confirmation of a particular upcoming event, price, opening time or availability; verify those details with the organiser before travelling.
activities.confidence: High for venue identity, address and programme description; medium for planning details because cost, schedule, age policy and entry requirements vary by event.
activities.official_source_title: The Workman's Club — Dublin's leading live entertainment venue

activities.name: St Anne's parkrun
activities.short_description: A free, friendly, volunteer-led 5k community event in St Anne's Park. Walk, jog, run, volunteer or spectate at your own pace.
activities.why_it_fits: It is a low-cost, beginner-friendly way for DCU students to get moving without needing a class booking: the 5k is open to different paces, and walking is explicitly welcome.
activities.location: St Anne's Park, Raheny, Dublin; meeting point and finish in the centre of the park near the eastern end of the main avenue.
activities.cost_basis: The official event page says joining is free and costs nothing; registration is required before a first visit.
activities.additional_potential_costs: Optional travel and post-event café purchases at Olive's Room; these are not part of the activity fee.
activities.approximate_duration: 5 km; completion time varies by pace. The event starts at 9:30am, with optional post-run coffee.
activities.availability: Every Saturday at 9:30am according to the official event page. Check the official page before travelling because schedules or individual events can change, including for special events or cancellations.
activities.booking_needed: No advance booking for each Saturday is stated, but register with parkrun before your first visit and bring the scannable barcode; no barcode means no recorded result.
best_suited_interests: meeting people through a community activity
activities.social_format: A welcoming group event organised by volunteers, with participants walking, jogging, running, volunteering or spectating together; optional post-run café meet-up.
activities.transport_suitability: Walking and cycling are suitable, and the organiser specifically encourages arriving by foot, bike or public transport. Public transport is suitable via Dublin Bus or DART to Raheny; driving is possible but parking may be limited.
activities.what_to_bring: A scannable parkrun barcode, comfortable running or walking clothes and shoes, and weather-appropriate layers. Bring water if useful; the course is on tarmac paths but can have mud, leaves or puddles after rain.
activities.caveat: The organiser says the course uses shared paths and may have uneven surfaces, mud, leaves or puddles after rain. Check the official page for the latest event status and bring a barcode for a timed result.
activities.official_source_title: St Anne’s parkrun — official parkrun Ireland event page

activities.name: Dublin Front Runners
activities.short_description: An LGBTQ+ running and social club with coached training, group runs for different abilities and distances, and a welcoming community atmosphere.
activities.why_it_fits: It combines exercise with a supportive social setting and offers varied paces, distances and coached sessions, making it a strong student option for getting active while meeting people.
activities.location: Multiple Dublin meeting points that change by season: Irishtown Stadium year-round; Papal Cross Car Park on Saturdays; and seasonal Wednesday/Monday locations including An Garda Síochána Headquarters, Phoenix Cricket Club and Magazine Fort.
activities.cost_basis: The official join page states annual membership is €56.50, so it does not fit the under-€40 bands; the fee covers 12 months from 1 January and is not prorated for late-year joining.
activities.additional_potential_costs: Transport, running gear and seasonal hi-vis clothing/head or body lamps may be additional; the organiser does not give prices for these.
activities.approximate_duration: Not stated by the organiser; allow time for the selected training or group-run session. Saturday runs are followed by optional breakfast and coffee.
activities.availability: The official page lists recurring Monday, Wednesday and Saturday sessions, but meeting points and routes vary by spring/summer versus autumn/winter. Confirm the current schedule and route with Dublin Front Runners before travelling, as details can change by date.
activities.booking_needed: Yes for club membership: complete the organiser’s registration form and pay the membership fee. The pages read do not specify separate session booking; contact the club to confirm the route and how a first visit should be arranged.
activities.energy_level: Moderate to high, with options for recreational joggers through experienced runners; a Saturday walking group is also described by the organiser.
best_suited_interests: LGBTQ+ community and ally-friendly social activities
activities.social_format: Group running with ambassadors, coaches and members at different paces and distances, plus socialising; Saturday sessions are followed by coffee and chats.
activities.transport_suitability: Public transport is a practical option, but the best route depends on the seasonal meeting point. Walking or cycling may suit some venues; check the exact route from DCU before going.
activities.what_to_bring: Comfortable running clothes and shoes; bring hi-vis clothing and a head/body lamp for autumn/winter runs as required by the organiser. Bring water and any personal essentials.
activities.caveat: This is a membership-based club, not a free drop-in class. The annual fee, schedule, routes and safety requirements should be rechecked with the organiser before attending.
activities.confidence: High for club identity, membership terms and listed seasonal locations; medium for date-specific availability because the organiser says routes and meeting points change by season.

activities.name: DCU Clubs and Societies
activities.short_description: Choose from DCU’s wide range of student clubs and societies, from sports and arts to culture, academic interests and hobbies. Joining gives you a natural way to meet people with shared interests on campus.
activities.why_it_fits: It is specifically designed around shared interests and group participation, making it an accessible way for a student to start conversations and build connections beyond their course.
activities.location: DCU campuses, with the main student-life hub at Glasnevin Campus, Dublin 9
activities.cost_basis: DCU lists many different clubs and societies, but the official directory does not state one universal membership price; costs depend on the individual club or society.
activities.additional_potential_costs: Some clubs or societies may have activity fees or costs for equipment, kit, trips, tickets or transport; check the individual organiser before committing.
activities.approximate_duration: Varies by club, society and event; individual meetings or activities may be short sessions or longer events.
activities.availability: Clubs and societies are offered across the academic year, but each group’s meetings, events, membership arrangements and activity schedule can change by date. Check the official directory and the individual organiser for current details.
activities.booking_needed: Varies by club or society. Use the official directory to identify the group and follow its registration or contact instructions; some activities may require advance sign-up.
activities.energy_level: Varies from low to high depending on the chosen club or society.
activities.social_format: Group-based and interest-led: attend meetings, training, events or activities with other DCU students.
activities.transport_suitability: Walking and cycling are suitable for on-campus activities. Public transport is suitable for reaching the DCU campus, but the exact venue and route vary by club or society.
activities.what_to_bring: Student ID if requested, comfortable clothes or any club-specific equipment, and a way to contact or register with the organiser.
activities.caveat: This is a directory of many different activities rather than one fixed event. Confirm the selected club or society’s current price, schedule, venue, availability and any requirements before attending.
activities.confidence: High for the overall activity and organiser; medium for cost, timing and exact venue because these vary by individual club or society.
activities.official_source_title: DCU Student Life — Search Clubs & Socs

activities.name: Page Turners Book Club
activities.short_description: A relaxed Dublin City Libraries reading group where adults discuss a chosen book and meet other readers.
activities.why_it_fits: It is a recurring, low-pressure way for a student to start conversations around a shared interest and build familiarity with other readers, rather than attending a one-off event alone.
activities.location: Central Library, Ilac Centre, Henry Street, Dublin 1
activities.cost_basis: The official Page Turners listing gives no participation price. Dublin City Libraries membership is free, but that does not establish that every club or event has no charge; confirm with Central Library.
activities.additional_potential_costs: Possible transport, printing, or buying the book; ask whether a library copy is available and whether any event-specific charge applies.
activities.availability: Meets on the first Monday of each month, 5:45–6:45pm. Dublin City Libraries says dates may change, so confirm the specific date and place with Central Library in advance.
activities.booking_needed: Not stated on the official event page. Email centrallibrary@dublincity.ie or phone 01 222 8300 to check space and joining arrangements before going.
best_suited_interests: Sharing opinions in a friendly group
activities.social_format: Small-group, in-person book discussion; contact Central Library for details before attending.
activities.transport_suitability: Public transport is suitable for this central-city venue; walking or cycling is also possible from DCU Glasnevin, depending on your route and preference. The library page links to Transport for Ireland timetables.
activities.what_to_bring: The book if you have it, plus your library card or photo ID if you need library services; bring questions or discussion points.
activities.caveat: The official listing confirms the recurring time and contact details but does not publish current book titles, capacity, a fee, or a booking rule. Check directly before attending because schedules and titles can change.
activities.official_source_title: Page Turners Book Club — Dublin City Council

activities.name: National Gallery of Ireland
activities.short_description: Explore Irish and European art in the National Gallery’s permanent collection, try a self-guided audio or themed tour on your phone, and make time for the Atrium Creative Space or a café stop.
activities.why_it_fits: It is a low-cost, flexible way for a DCU student to try something new without committing to a class or fixed event: visit independently, join a free tour if one is scheduled, or use the Gallery’s self-guided resources.
activities.location: National Gallery of Ireland, Merrion Square West and Clare Street, Dublin city centre
activities.cost_basis: The official visitor guide and opening-hours page state that admission to the permanent collection is free and no booking is required; some temporary exhibitions charge separately.
activities.additional_potential_costs: Optional costs may include a ticket for a paid temporary exhibition, café food or drinks, and transport. Prices vary; check the Gallery and transport providers before going.
activities.approximate_duration: Flexible self-guided visit; choose anything from a short drop-in to a longer gallery visit.
activities.availability: The Gallery states it is open seven days a week: Monday 11:00–17:30; Tuesday–Wednesday 09:15–17:30; Thursday 09:15–20:30; Friday–Saturday 09:15–17:30; Sunday 11:00–17:30. Hours are subject to change, entry ends 15 minutes before closing, and some rooms may close temporarily. Check the official page before visiting on your chosen date.
activities.booking_needed: No booking is required for the permanent collection or many free temporary exhibitions. Groups must book a visit time slot, and some temporary exhibitions require tickets.
activities.social_format: Good solo activity or relaxed small-group outing; easy to browse at your own pace.
activities.transport_suitability: Public transport, walking and cycling are suitable. The Gallery says it is in the city centre, less than 10 minutes on foot from St Stephen’s Green, Grafton Street and Trinity College, with nearby DART, LUAS, bus and Dublinbikes options. From DCU Glasnevin, public transport or cycling is the practical choice; no precise journey time is claimed.
activities.what_to_bring: A phone and headphones for audio descriptions or self-guided tours, plus comfortable shoes. Avoid bringing luggage larger than a handheld bag or regular backpack that fits the Gallery’s lockers.
activities.caveat: Free admission applies to the permanent collection, not necessarily every temporary exhibition. Tour schedules, room access, opening hours and exhibition charges can change by date; verify the official What’s On and visitor pages before travelling.
activities.official_source_title: National Gallery of Ireland — Visitor Guide

activities.name: Irish Museum of Modern Art (IMMA)
activities.short_description: Explore contemporary art in the historic Royal Hospital Kilmainham, then wander IMMA’s galleries, formal gardens and 48-acre grounds. It is a flexible, low-cost outing that works well with friends or on your own.
activities.why_it_fits: It is a genuinely different Dublin experience for a student: free general entry, an unusual historic setting, contemporary art to spark conversation, and outdoor space to extend the visit without needing a tightly scheduled plan.
activities.location: Royal Hospital Kilmainham, Military Road, Dublin 8, D08 FW31, Ireland
activities.cost_basis: IMMA’s official visitor information says admission is free and most exhibitions are free.
activities.additional_potential_costs: Optional café or shop spending; parking is paid. Some special events or exhibitions may have separate terms, so check the relevant IMMA listing.
activities.approximate_duration: Allow about 1–3 hours, depending on how much of the galleries and grounds you explore.
activities.availability: IMMA’s normal visitor information says it is open six days a week and closed Mondays except Bank Holidays; listed hours are Tue/Thu–Sat 10:00–17:30, Wed 11:30–17:30, Sun and Bank Holidays 12:00–17:30, with last gallery admission at 17:15. Hours, exhibitions and access arrangements can change by date—verify before going.
activities.booking_needed: No booking is normally needed for general admission. Check IMMA’s official programme page before travelling if you want a tour, workshop, special event or particular exhibition.
activities.social_format: Good solo or with friends; easy to browse at your own pace and meet up for the grounds or café.
activities.transport_suitability: Public transport and cycling are suitable; walking is possible but likely a longer option from DCU Glasnevin. Use a live journey planner for the route and current timetables.
activities.what_to_bring: Student ID if useful for other discounts, a phone, water, and weather-appropriate layers; comfortable shoes help for the galleries and grounds.
activities.caveat: This is a date-sensitive planning snapshot. Confirm opening hours, exhibition access, tours/events, and any special charges on the official IMMA site immediately before visiting.
activities.confidence: High — based primarily on the official IMMA visitor-information page, with transport context cross-checked against Transport for Ireland.

activities.name: Govinda's
activities.short_description: A relaxed Dublin city-centre vegetarian kitchen serving fresh daily specials plus a fixed menu of rice, dhal, paneer curry and tofu curry. Vegan choices are available, and the menu changes by day.
activities.why_it_fits: It is a straightforward, student-friendly food stop with vegetarian and vegan choices, city-centre access, a relaxed social setting and meal options that fit an under-€20 budget.
activities.location: 83 Middle Abbey Street, Dublin 1, D01 EV91
activities.cost_basis: The official site displays an indicative €10–20 per person; the read Deliveroo menu lists meal options at €8.50 and €12.95, supporting an under-€20 food budget before extras or delivery fees.
activities.additional_potential_costs: Drinks and extras cost more; the read menu lists drinks from €2.50 and some drinks at €4.00. Delivery fees may apply if ordering online.
activities.approximate_duration: About 30–60 minutes for a casual meal; this is a planning estimate, not a venue-stated duration.
activities.availability: The official page showed daily service when checked: Sun 12:00–18:00, Mon–Thu 12:00–19:00, and Fri–Sat 12:00–20:00. Hours, menu and service may change by date, so check the official page before travelling.
activities.booking_needed: No booking requirement is stated on the official page. Plan for a walk-in visit, and contact the venue first if you need certainty about seating or dietary requirements.
activities.social_format: Casual dine-in or takeaway; suitable for going solo or with a small group. The venue describes cosy corners and a welcoming atmosphere.
activities.transport_suitability: Public transport and cycling are suitable for reaching the city centre. Walking from DCU Glasnevin is possible but is a substantial cross-city walk; no precise journey time is claimed.
activities.what_to_bring: Payment method, and an allergy or dietary checklist if needed; ask staff about daily specials and ingredients because dishes rotate.
activities.caveat: Govinda's is explicitly vegetarian rather than necessarily fully vegan: the official site lists both vegetarian and vegan dishes, and the menu rotates. The official page does not establish a dedicated coffee offering, so confirm drinks and dietary details before visiting.
activities.confidence: High for venue identity, location, food style and indicative cost; medium for exact hours and current prices because these can change.

activities.name: Boojum — Kevin Street
activities.short_description: A casual Mexican burrito bar where you can customise a burrito, bowl or salad with rice, beans, fillings, salsas and extras. Good for a quick solo meal or an easy catch-up with friends.
activities.why_it_fits: It is a real, accessible Dublin food stop with a central listed venue, customisable mains, vegetarian options and a price point that can fit a student budget. It is easy to frame as a low-effort meal or small-group meet-up rather than a time-fixed event.
activities.location: College Court, Kevin Street Lower, Portobello, Dublin D08 A440
activities.cost_basis: The Kevin Street Deliveroo menu read on 2026-10-08 lists burritos, bowls and salads at €10.55, with meal deals from €12.25 and several mains up to €16.25; delivery-platform prices may differ from in-store prices.
activities.additional_potential_costs: Optional drinks, sides, guacamole, queso and other extras cost more; the listing shows drinks from €2.55 and sides from €3.05. Delivery fees do not apply if eating in or collecting in person.
activities.approximate_duration: 30–60 minutes for ordering and eating; this is a planning estimate, not a venue-published duration.
activities.availability: The official Boojum locator lists Kevin Street as open Monday–Sunday, 11:30am–10:00pm. Hours, service and menu availability can change, so verify on the official locator before setting out.
activities.booking_needed: No booking is normally needed for a casual meal; walk in or use Boojum’s ordering/Click 'N Collect options. A queue may form at busy times.
activities.social_format: Casual drop-in; works for solo dining, a pair or a small student group. Seating and queueing can vary at busy times.
activities.transport_suitability: Suitable for walking, cycling and public transport once in central Dublin. From DCU Glasnevin, public transport or cycling is more practical than treating it as a short walk; check a live route before travelling.
activities.what_to_bring: Payment method and, if using a student offer, valid student ID; bring a phone if ordering Click 'N Collect. Check dietary and allergen information before ordering.
activities.caveat: Boojum is primarily a Mexican burrito bar rather than a coffee-focused venue. The official menu page did not expose prices in the text read, so the cost band is based on the read Kevin Street Deliveroo listing and should not be treated as a guaranteed in-store price.
activities.confidence: High for the venue address, concept and listed hours; medium for current prices and exact in-store availability because the price evidence is a delivery listing and both menus and hours can change.

activities.name: National Botanic Gardens of Ireland
activities.short_description: Explore free outdoor gardens and historic glasshouses in Glasnevin, with plant collections from around the world and a calm break from campus.
activities.why_it_fits: It is genuinely free, outdoors, student-friendly, and in Glasnevin near DCU. It offers a flexible low-cost plan for a quiet walk, nature break, or informal group meetup without committing to a class or scheduled event.
activities.location: National Botanic Gardens, Botanic Road, Glasnevin, Dublin
activities.cost_basis: The official Gardens site states there is no admission fee to walk and explore the Glasnevin gardens.
activities.additional_potential_costs: Optional guided tours usually cost €5; the café, shop, and paid car parking are extra. Parking is charged by the hour and is limited at busy times.
activities.approximate_duration: About 1.5 hours (Heritage Ireland lists the average visit length); allow longer for a slower walk or glasshouse stops.
activities.availability: Open throughout the year except Christmas Day, but opening hours are seasonal and can change. Check the official opening-hours page before travelling, especially around public holidays or events.
activities.booking_needed: No booking is needed for ordinary individual garden entry. Groups of more than 10 must book in advance; guided tours are optional and paid.
activities.social_format: Good for a casual solo visit, relaxed pair, or small student group; self-guided and easy to explore at your own pace.
activities.transport_suitability: Suitable for walking, cycling, and public transport. The Gardens provide bicycle parking but cycling is not allowed inside the grounds; paths are generally broad with all-weather surfaces, though some steps exist.
activities.what_to_bring: Weather-appropriate layers and comfortable shoes; bring water and a phone for maps. A rain jacket is sensible for Dublin weather.
activities.caveat: Free entry applies to the Gardens themselves; guided tours and on-site purchases are separate. Do not assume a specific tour time, opening hour, or event is available without checking the official site on the day.
activities.official_source_title: National Botanic Gardens of Ireland — official website

activities.name: Howth Cliff Path Loop (Howth Head)
activities.short_description: A self-guided coastal loop from Howth village, following the harbour to clifftop paths with wide views across Dublin Bay, Lambay Island, Ireland’s Eye and Baily Lighthouse.
activities.why_it_fits: It is genuinely free at the point of activity, outdoors, student-friendly, reachable from DCU Glasnevin by public transport, and offers a clear two-hour route with scenic and social walking appeal.
activities.location: Howth Village and Howth Head, Dublin; start and finish at Howth Railway Station
activities.cost_basis: The listed activity is a self-guided walking trail with no admission or booking fee stated by the official activity page; local transport is not included.
activities.additional_potential_costs: DART or other transport from DCU, plus optional food, drinks or café stops in Howth; fares and purchases vary by date and choice.
activities.approximate_duration: About 2 hours for the 7.8 km loop; allow extra time for stops, photos and getting to/from DCU.
activities.availability: A self-guided outdoor route that is generally usable year-round, but weather, ground conditions, maintenance or temporary access changes can affect the experience. Confirm current conditions before going.
activities.booking_needed: No booking is needed for the self-guided public trail; check current route information before travel.
activities.energy_level: Moderate: a 7.8 km loop with some ascent, rough ground and exposed coastal sections.
activities.social_format: Good for a small group, walking club or casual pair; it is self-guided rather than a scheduled class or tour.
activities.transport_suitability: Walking and cycling are suitable for reaching the area if you are prepared for a longer approach; public transport is the most practical student option, with the loop starting at Howth Railway Station. The clifftop trail is a moderate walk, with rough sections and 130 m aggregate ascent.
activities.what_to_bring: Comfortable walking shoes or boots, water, weatherproof layers, and a phone; bring extra layers for wind and check conditions before setting out.
activities.caveat: The official page describes the trail, not a guaranteed live access status or DCU-to-Howth itinerary. Transport fares, weather, path conditions and access can change; do not treat the approximate duration as total trip time.
activities.confidence: High for route distance, duration, start/finish and terrain because these come from the official Visit Dublin listing; medium for transport and variable conditions.
activities.official_source_title: Visit Dublin — Howth - Cliff Path Loop

activities.name: National Museum of Ireland – Archaeology
activities.short_description: Explore Ireland’s archaeological story in the museum’s historic Kildare Street galleries, from prehistoric gold and Neolithic objects to Viking finds, medieval treasures and bog bodies. It is a free, self-guided cultural visit—but the activity itself is indoors, not outdoors.
activities.why_it_fits: It is a genuinely free, flexible Dublin activity with strong student appeal: central location, no booking for a small outing, and enough varied collections to suit history, archaeology, art and heritage interests. It works well as a low-cost social plan, although it should not be presented as an outdoor activity.
activities.location: Archaeology, Kildare Street, Dublin 2, D02 FH48
activities.cost_basis: The official National Museum of Ireland visitor page states that admission to all four museum sites is free.
activities.additional_potential_costs: Transport to and from Dublin city centre, optional purchases in the museum shop or nearby food, and paid parking may cost extra; no ticket purchase is required for ordinary individual entry.
activities.approximate_duration: About 1–2 hours as a flexible student visit; allow longer if reading exhibits closely. This is a planning estimate, not a published timed session.
activities.availability: The official page lists Tuesday–Saturday 10am–5pm and Sunday–Monday 1pm–5pm, with some seasonal Thursday late openings. It also lists Christmas Day, St Stephen’s Day and Good Friday closures and warns that galleries can close at short notice. Confirm current hours and any closure before travelling on 2026-10-08.
activities.booking_needed: Not for individuals, families or small social units. Groups of 8 or more must book in advance; the official page says self-guided group visits can be booked at least 7 days ahead. Contact bookings@museum.ie for group, school or special-interest options.
activities.energy_level: Low to moderate: mostly standing and walking indoors at your own pace.
best_suited_interests: Art, material culture and historic objects
activities.social_format: Self-guided and easy to do solo, as a pair, or with a small group; use the galleries as conversation prompts. Groups of 8 or more must book in advance with the Museum.
activities.transport_suitability: Public transport is the most practical option from DCU Glasnevin; cycling is also suitable for confident city cyclists. Walking is possible but is a relatively long urban trip, so do not plan around a precise journey time without checking a live route.
activities.what_to_bring: A phone or notebook for exhibit notes, comfortable shoes, and a small bag. The Museum says cloakroom services are currently unavailable, so avoid suitcases, motorcycle helmets and large bags; handheld photography is allowed for personal use, but flash, video and tripods are not permitted.
activities.caveat: The supplied category says “Free and outdoors,” but the National Museum of Ireland – Archaeology is an indoor museum. Regular hours and particular gallery access may change, and the official source recommends checking ahead if a specific artefact or exhibition is important.
activities.confidence: High for venue, address, collections, free admission and booking rules; medium for day-of availability because the Museum warns that hours and gallery access can change.
activities.official_source_title: National Museum of Ireland – Archaeology: Opening Hours, Location and Facilities
